title: Restoring Linguistic Grounding in VLA Models via Train-Free Attention Recalibration
action_head: mixed: flow/diffusion action expert (pi0, pi0.5) and regression head (OpenVLA-OFT parallel decoding)
methods: ICBench: LIBERO tasks with contradictory instructions (operand attribute, target attribute, both, spatial relation) and unchanged scenes
Linguistic Grounding Score LGS = SR(normal) - SR(contradictory)
IGAR: attention-sink detection via hidden-state spike ratio, head selection by visual-sink share, redistribution of attention from sink tokens to non-sink instruction tokens in the first 16 layers
question: Do VLAs ignore language when the instruction contradicts the scene, and can rebalancing attention toward instruction tokens restore language influence without retraining?
key_findings: Linguistic blindness: under contradictory instructions success often stays above 90%; e.g. pi0.5 Spatial V1 96.2% (LGS 1.2), OpenVLA-OFT Object V3 99.8% (LGS -1.4); pi0 is least blind (Goal V4 SR 76.4%, LGS 19.4) (Table 1, 50 rollouts per task variant).
IGAR raises LGS most for pi0 and OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO-Goal: pi0 V4 SR 36.4%, LGS 59.4; OpenVLA-OFT V4 SR 58.4%, LGS 39.6; on Spatial and Object, LGS mostly stays in the 2-20 range (Table 2).
pi0.5 barely changes: Goal V1 LGS 3.8 -> 7.4; Spatial V4 LGS -2.2 after IGAR.
Normal-instruction success is largely preserved: average change -0.4 (pi0), -1.5 (pi0.5, including -4.0 on Object), +0.5 (OpenVLA-OFT) points (Table 3).
Component ablation (pi0.5, Goal V1): attention-to-text 0.08 -> 0.15 and LGS 3.8 -> 7.4 with full IGAR; removing sink detection gives 4.6, removing head selection 4.2.
Latency for OpenVLA-OFT rises from 98.7 to 105.6 ms per step.
Real Franka (pi0, one cube-in-drawer task): baseline completes contradicted instructions ('fake success'), IGAR produces hovering or empty grasps; reported qualitatively.

evidence.setting: both (LIBERO simulation; one real Franka task, qualitative)
benchmarks: ICBench built on LIBERO-Spatial, -Object, -Goal (30 tasks, 4 contradiction types)
evidence.scale: 50 rollouts per task variant; real-robot trial count not reported
evidence.baselines: unmodified VLAs; component ablations of IGAR; no competing grounding or attention-intervention baseline

causal_validation: Yes in a limited sense: modifying attention weights changes closed-loop behavior under contradictory instructions, and a component ablation is reported. But the outcome metric (lower success) cannot distinguish restored grounding from generic disruption of the policy when instructions are unusual.
closed_loop: Yes, all success rates are closed-loop LIBERO rollouts.
limitations_stated: Not stated as a separate section in the text read; the hyperparameter section notes that intervening in too many layers (L > 24) corrupts action representations.
critique: LGS rewards any failure under contradiction, so a perturbation that makes the policy fragile under unfamiliar instructions would also score well. A 'correct' grounded behavior (abstain, stop, ask) is never measured; the real-robot 'hovering or empty grasps' is closer to breakage than refusal.
The method applied to pi0 is a different 'contrastive' formulation from the sink-redistribution IGAR used for pi0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT, yet pi0 provides the headline gains.
Hyperparameters were tuned on OpenVLA-OFT LIBERO-Goal, the same benchmark used for evaluation; gains are concentrated on Goal and weak on Spatial/Object.
No random-head or random-redistribution control, so it is unclear whether attending more to text specifically, or just perturbing attention, drives the LGS increase.

The diagnostic finding (VLAs often complete tasks under impossible instructions on LIBERO) is the stronger contribution and agrees with other papers that report weak language dependence on LIBERO (2610.10178, 2604.18000).
code: project page https://ray-nh.github.io/igar/ (code status not stated)
one_line: On LIBERO, pi0, pi0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT still complete tasks when the instruction names absent objects or impossible relations, and shifting attention mass from sink tokens to instruction tokens makes pi0 and OpenVLA-OFT fail more often under such contradictions with little cost on normal instructions.
